topStories.headline: Record Rainstorm Pounds These Neighborhoods — Muni Rerouted, I-280 Floods at Glen Park's Edge
topStories.dek: An atmospheric river dumped nearly twice November's normal rainfall on San Francisco in a single morning on November 18, flooding roads, knocking out power, and disrupting Muni lines that serve these neighborhoods.
topStories.body:
A powerful atmospheric river swept through the Bay Area on Wednesday, November 18, breaking a rainfall record for San Francisco that had stood since 1918. The city received roughly 4.36 inches of rain — well above the full-month November average of 2.60 inches — in just a matter of hours, according to National Weather Service data cited by the SF Chronicle.

The flooding hit close to home. Interstate 280, which runs along the eastern edge of Glen Park, saw more than a foot of water standing in its southbound lanes near Geneva Avenue at around 10:35 a.m., according to the California Highway Patrol. The SFMTA rerouted the M Ocean View line onto the K Ingleside alignment due to flooding at 19th Avenue, adding travel time for riders connecting to the Castro and Noe Valley.

Strong winds accompanied the deluge, with gusts forecast to reach 40 mph in coastal areas of the city. PG&E reported outages affecting tens of thousands of homes and businesses regionwide, though the worst effects had eased by Thursday. San Francisco's Recreation and Parks Department temporarily closed Stern Grove — a facility used heavily by Glen Park and Diamond Heights residents — along with the Botanical Garden and Japanese Tea Garden in Golden Gate Park, pending staff safety inspections.

Forecasters warned that another cold front was expected to approach the region over the weekend, keeping the threat of additional rain and localized flooding in place into next week. Residents with electric vehicles were also cautioned by San Francisco officials about the fire risk posed by saltwater exposure following street flooding.

topStories.headline: Supervisor-Elect McCoy Waits for December Count — Here Is What He Has Said He Will Do First
topStories.dek: Gary McCoy won the District 8 race on November 3 and is now supervisor-elect, but he will not be seated until the results are officially certified next month.
topStories.body:
Gary McCoy declared victory on November 3 in the race to represent District 8 — the supervisor seat covering the Castro, Noe Valley, Duboce Triangle, Glen Park, and Cole Valley — defeating Darshini Patel. McCoy received 24,252 votes after ranked-choice tabulation, to Patel's 10,846 first-choice votes, according to the SF Standard.

McCoy, a former aide to both Supervisor Scott Wiener and Congressmember Nancy Pelosi, and later a top official at HealthRIGHT 360, the city's largest addiction treatment provider, is replacing termed-out Supervisor Rafael Mandelman. He is set to maintain the district's 25-year streak of representation by an openly gay man. McCoy received endorsements from across the political spectrum, including from housing advocacy groups and labor organizations, suggesting he could serve as a swing vote on a Board of Supervisors that has largely aligned with Mayor Daniel Lurie.

McCoy has spoken publicly about his own history with addiction and recovery, and has indicated those experiences will shape his approach to homelessness and the drug crisis. He has also expressed support for the SFPD drone program with what he has described as appropriate guardrails, and has said he intends to introduce legislation to end the city's conservatorship expansion within his first 90 days in office.

The November 3 results are not yet certified. San Francisco typically certifies election results in December, at which point McCoy will be formally sworn in. Until then, Mandelman remains the seated supervisor for District 8.

topStories.headline: Castro Farmers' Market Closes for the Season After Its Final Wednesday on Noe Street
topStories.dek: The Castro Farmers' Market held its last market day of 2026 on November 18, ending a season that ran from April through mid-November.
topStories.body:
The Castro Farmers' Market wrapped up its 2026 outdoor season on Wednesday, November 18, with one final gathering on Noe Street. The market, which opened in April, ran weekly on Wednesdays and drew neighbors, local farmers, and small food producers throughout the spring, summer, and fall.

The season's close was noted by the San Francisco Bay Times, which reported that community leaders including Donna Sachet and representatives of the Castro Merchants Association had participated in this year's market events. The market serves as an informal gathering point for the neighborhood — a place where, as organizers have put it, the purpose extends beyond what happens to be in season.

No return date for the 2027 season has been publicly announced. Shoppers looking for local produce and artisan goods in the interim can still find the Noe Valley Farmers' Market, which runs Saturdays at 3861–3865 24th Street from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., through its own seasonal schedule.

moreNews.headline: Glen Park Holiday Gift Drive Runs Through December 1
moreNews.body: OTTP-NorCal, a mental health nonprofit serving youth in the area, launched its annual Holiday Gift Drive on November 2 and is accepting gift sponsorships through December 1. Sponsors choose gifts selected by the young people themselves — ranging from sensory toys that support therapy to LEGOs and new shoes — for youth who face financial hardship. Since 2020, community members have funded gifts this way. To sponsor a gift, visit roonga.com/hgd26; general donations can be made at ottpnc.org/donate by selecting 'Holiday Gift Drive.' The drive was listed on the Glen Park Association's website on November 1, 2026.

moreNews.headline: Castro Retail Turnover Continues: Fave Closed in September, New Studios Opening on Noe
moreNews.body: The Castro's retail picture continued to shift this fall. Fave, the queer mall and screen-printing shop at 329 Noe Street, closed on September 26 after less than three years, with the owner citing high rent and insufficient foot traffic; screen printing moves to Treasure Island. On the opening side, the former Noe and Market Laundromat at 262 Noe Street has reopened as Bisk Studio, a pottery and jewelry space, according to the Bay Area Reporter. These changes were reported by Hoodline and the Bay Area Reporter in October–November 2026.
